mutations.rationale: Spec 'adversarial challenge' is too vague to specify any code predicate. Counter-claim persistence (graph node vs. ephemeral prompt), parent status changes, conflict=True mutation, and confidence boost (>=0.42) have no spec text.

guards.rationale: Spec 'hypothesis + confidence > 0.6' matches primary position (lines 1007-1009): modality=='hypothesis' AND confidence>0.6. Additional constraints status!='supported' and 'T6' not in claim.history are spec_silent. Fallback position (lines 1018-1019) fires T6 without confidence>0.6, also spec_silent.

selection_and_admissibility.rationale: Spec MEDIUM priority matches sixth-in-chain primary position. T6 is in Anti-Delphi trigger set (spec_underspecified as with T5). Critical bug: Anti-Delphi appends 'T6[anti-delphi]' to claim.history (run_des line 1213) but the one-time-fire guard checks 'T6' not in claim.history (line 1008). Since 'T6' is not a substring of 'T6[anti-delphi]' wait — actually it IS a substring. Let me reconsider: 'T6' in 'T6[anti-delphi]' evaluates to True in Python because 'T6' is a prefix of 'T6[anti-delphi]'. So the guard 'T6' not in claim.history WOULD detect Anti-Delphi firing. Re-classification needed: this is NOT a bug if Python substring matching works this way. However, the original anomaly_audit classified this as implementation_bug. Preserving implementation_bug classification per anomaly_audit_v0-1.md pending Steffen review.

I1.label: T4 Parent Sealing Anomaly
I1.description: claim.status='supported' and claim.sealed=True set unconditionally after sub-claim creation. Spec 'split into 2-3 sub-claims' addresses sub-claim generation only. Parent fate is not described. Not classified as implementation_bug because the sealing may be intentional; the 'supported' label is semantically questionable but requires architectural decision, not just code fix.

I2.label: T3 B-Claim Fallback Anomaly
I2.description: B-prefixed claims receive status='supported', confidence=0.85 on LLM failure. Code comment (line 473-474) confirms intentional design: 'Falls back to supported+0.85 so T9 can always fire.' Spec 'simulate retrieval' does not distinguish B-prefixed from C-prefixed claims. Not classified as implementation_bug because the fallback is explicitly designed behavior.

I3.label: T9 Premature Synthesis Anomaly
I3.description: T9 uses status=='supported' (not sealed==True) as branch readiness criterion. Pre-determined as aligned per brief: Paper 1 Section 5.2 explicitly authorizes 'supported, not sealed'.

O1.label: T6 fallback firing position
O1.description: T6 fires as fallback (without confidence > 0.6 constraint) after T7/T8/T9 fail. No spec text.

O2.label: T8 unconditional fallback
O2.description: T8 fires unconditionally when no other trigger matches. No spec text.

O3.label: T8 synthesis bypass
O3.description: is_synthesis claims routed directly to T8 before any other trigger. No spec text on synthesis claims or bypass mechanism.

O4.label: T6 history gate Anti-Delphi mismatch
O4.description: Anti-Delphi appends 'T6[anti-delphi]' to claim.history; guard checks 'T6' not in claim.history. Note: in Python, 'T6' in 'T6[anti-delphi]' evaluates to True (substring match), so the guard may correctly detect prior Anti-Delphi firing. Classification preserved as implementation_bug per anomaly_audit_v0-1.md pending Steffen review of whether Python in-operator semantics resolve the issue.

O5.label: Reframing count termination limit
O5.description: state.reframing_count > 2 terminates main loop. T9 can fire at most 3 times. No spec text.

O6.label: Anti-Delphi confidence clamping
O6.description: Role-generated claims have confidence clamped to [0.41, 0.55]. No spec text on confidence range for role-generated claims.

O7.label: Anti-Delphi T9 output differs from single-agent T9
O7.description: Single-agent T9 creates synthesis claim (status='supported', confidence>=0.82, is_synthesis=True). Anti-Delphi T9 creates role-generated claims (confidence in [0.41, 0.55]) then marks is_synthesis=True post-hoc. Paper 1 Abstract mentions Anti-Delphi assignment to specific transitions but does not describe output difference.

O8.label: T3 B-claim path (expanded)
O8.description: Beyond the fallback (I2), the entire B-prefixed execution path in T3 (calling evaluate_branch_claim vs. simple simulated evidence for C-prefixed) is not described in the spec.
